doc.name: A — protein powder catalogue, retail shelf, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: whey isolate tub and scoop
Category: protein powder
Shot programme: retail shelf
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the visual lead responsible for this protein powder product library. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the split-level stack in a retail shelf treatment.

SUBJECT. A whey isolate tub and scoop. Product fidelity is non-negotiable: shape, seams, cap, closure, print placement and colour must match the reference precisely. Only the scene around it is yours to author.

CAMERA. Product on a stepped plinth arrangement at two heights. Shoot on a 135mm telephoto at f/1.4, framing for leading lines converging on the subject from the lower corners.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with an overcast soft dome with no directional shadow at all. Stage the product on or against seamless paper sweep, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a clean high-key grade with the whites pushed to the edge of clipping. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Your entire reply is the prompt itself: one dense paragraph, no title, no quotation marks, no trailing notes.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
